1.explanation: All of the wrapping behavior (or lack thereof) lives in the CodeSnippet component implementation in CodeSnippet.js. The main function, CodeSnippet, is responsible for rendering the <pre> element and assembling its class names; it needs to be updated to accept a new wrapText prop, to apply a CSS class (or inline style) that enables word-wrapping on the <pre>. The static propTypes and defaultProps definitions must also be extended to declare wrapText and its default value. By modifying only CodeSnippet.js (its component logic, propTypes, and defaultProps), we can add the wrapText feature without touching unrelated files.
1.bug_scenario: The user is embedding a very long, single‐line string (a CRN URI) in a <CodeSnippet type="multi"> component inside a narrow container (300px wide). Because the component does not currently support text wrapping, the long line overflows its box horizontally and triggers a scroll bar rather than breaking onto multiple lines.

2.explanation: The CodeSnippet component (in CodeSnippet.js) is the central render function that wraps the code in a <pre> tag and applies CSS classes via the codeSnippetClasses variable. It currently does not recognise a wrapText prop, and the default white-space styling of <pre> prevents line breaks, causing overflow. To enable wrapping, CodeSnippet must be updated to accept a wrapText prop, extend its propTypes/defaultProps, and adjust codeSnippetClasses (or inline style) to apply a CSS rule (e.g. white-space: pre-wrap) when wrapText is true. Hence, the CodeSnippet function and its className logic are the key areas to modify.
2.bug_scenario: In a multi-line CodeSnippet containing a long single-line string (a CRN), the text does not wrap inside its container but instead overflows and introduces a horizontal scrollbar. The user wants a wrapText prop to enable automatic word-wrapping so that the long string breaks onto multiple lines within the set width.
